note: The first input byte selects the target architecture; choosing TMS320C64X routes execution into the vulnerable backend.
The selected platform opens a Capstone handle configured for TMS320C64X disassembly.

code: fprintf(outfile, "0x%"PRIx64":\t%s\t\t%s // insn-ID: %u, insn-mnem: %s\n", i->address, i->mnemonic, i->op_str, i->id, cs_insn_name(handle, i->id));
note: Printing the decoded instruction name calls into the backend name lookup with the decoded instruction id.
The backend only checks id against TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING, but the sparse insn_name_maps table contains far fewer entries, so a valid id can index past the table and read out of bounds.
